overall: Committee violated the OML by failing to periodically review executive session minutes for release and was ordered to release December 20, 2018 executive session materials within 30 days; footnoted allegations declined. Reissued Dec 7 to clarify the 2018 purpose violation was found in OML 2019-161.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to periodically review its executive session minutes for release.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that the Committee periodically reviewed its executive session minutes for possible release to the public, and the Committee has provided none.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to release documents, exhibits, notes and recordings used for the December 20, 2018 executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee lacked a proper purpose for meeting in executive session on December 20, 2018, the Committee must release to the public any documents and exhibits used during the December 20, 2018, executive session, as well as any notes, recordings or other materials used in the preparation of the December 20, 2018, executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the December 20, 2018 executive session lacked a proper purpose; the AG had already found a violation in OML 2019-161 and did not reconsider.
allegations.key_passage: As we have already found the Committee in violation of the Open Meeting Law in this regard, we do not reconsider this allegation here.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee's meeting minutes do not appear on the Committee's website; declined as not an Open Meeting Law violation.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, these allegations would not constitute violations of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the December 20, 2018 executive session minutes were improperly redacted under the Public Records Law; declined as outside Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, these allegations would not constitute violations of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged Committee members were instructed by the Committee's attorneys not to communicate with the complainant; declined as outside Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, these allegations would not constitute violations of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
Review all executive session minutes in compliance with the letter's guidance.

Release, within 30 days of receipt, the documents and exhibits used during the December 20, 2018 executive session and any notes, recordings or other materials used in preparing its minutes, without redaction.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
